# PUMA Analyzer

> PUMA Analyzer is a Windows desktop application that estimates thin-film
> thickness and optical constants (refractive index n, extinction
> coefficient k) from a measured transmission spectrum, using a
> physics-based transmittance model and a compiled C nonlinear-optimization
> engine. It is proprietary software gated by an activation code, not
> open source; this repository hosts only release binaries and the
> update-check manifest, no source code.

## Key facts

- Platform: Windows 10+ (64-bit) only.
- Core engine: `puma_seq.exe`, compiled from `puma_seq.c`, implementing
  the unconstrained-optimization thin-film parameter estimation method
  of Birgin, Chambouleyron and Martinez.
- Physical model: T(lambda) = A*x / (B - C*x*cos(phi) + D*x^2), with
  x = exp(-4*pi*k*d/lambda) and phi = 4*pi*n*d/lambda.
- Derives dozens of further quantities from the fit: optical band gap
  (Tauc, direct/indirect), Urbach energy, Wemple-DiDomenico dispersion,
  dielectric function, Kramers-Kronig consistency check, and more.
- License/activation: requires a one-time activation code (name, email,
  code) verified against a server; no spectra or project data is ever
  transmitted.
- Not open source: proprietary, Copyright Amin Al-Zu'bi.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): full description, physics equations, screenshots,
  a downloadable sample dataset with step-by-step instructions, FAQ,
  and version history.
- [Releases](https://github.com/ameenalzubi0-bit/puma-analyzer-releases/releases):
  downloadable Windows builds and per-version release notes.
